title: Book Three · Chapter 59: The Book in the Other City
story:
At the start of the third week, Leo's ninth reply arrives.

Ronan reads it at home before dinner. The first part is about the new school term. Leo has longer questions too. His fast friend still hates the written parts.

Then Ronan reaches the book.

I found it. The larger library has it. My aunt looked at another book about the old city. She found her old street in a picture.

Ronan reads the next lines twice.

The station in Anna's book has a low roof. Our station's roof is much higher. I borrowed the book, so I can look again. I will take it back with my aunt.

At the bottom, Leo has drawn two simple roofs. One is nearly flat. The other curves in the middle.

Ronan takes a clean sheet and copies both. He writes Book above one and Leo's station above the other.

The next morning, he gives Anna the sheet before class.

“He found it.”

She looks up at once.

“The same book?”

“Yes. He borrowed it. His aunt found her old street too.”

Anna studies the two roofs. Then she takes out her own notebook.

“Can I keep this?”

“That copy is yours.”

She asks about the two labels. Ronan reads Leo's words from the letter. Anna adds a note below the curved roof, so she can keep the two buildings apart.

She puts it beside the hall drawings. Lin comes over and looks at it too.

“The roof really is different,” Lin says.

Anna nods. “I want to see the inside of that station one day.”

Ronan thinks of Leo's invitation. A trip still needs money, family dates, and a place to stay.

“I need to ask at home first,” he says.

Anna looks at him and smiles.

“Not today. One day.”

The teacher comes in, and the girls put the drawings away.

At lunch, Ronan tells Kai about the book. Kai wants to know about Leo's new friend.

“Still fast?”

“Still bad at throwing.”

“Good. I can visit.”

Ronan laughs. Then Kai asks about a line in his science answer. Ronan listens as he reads it aloud.

This time, the sentence has a beginning and an end. One word is in the wrong place, but Ronan can follow it.

“Say that bit again,” he asks.

Kai does. He hears the wrong word himself and moves it.

After school, Anna gives Ronan a small folded paper. She has copied her drawing from inside the hall.

“For Leo,” she says. “My window for his roof.”

Ronan opens it carefully. The wide window sits above the clear doorway.

At home, he puts it beside the ninth reply and takes out a new sheet. His answer can carry a better drawing this time.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

borrow＝借来；nearly flat＝近乎平的；curve＝弯曲；copy＝一份副本、复制的图。

## 理解问题

1. Leo有没有找到建筑书？姨妈在图书馆有没有自己的兴趣？
2. Anna得到的是Leo的原信还是Ronan复制的图？她后来怎样回应？

## 读句子

**That copy is yours.**

拆开看：That copy / is / yours.

那张复制的图／是／你的。
